findings.title: Applet progress can be forged over plain HTTP
findings.entry_point: A server-controlled or intercepted response from http://www.apo-games.de/apoRelax/cookies.php during applet startup. ApoRelaxApplet.java:27-29 enables applet mode and ApoRelaxApplet.java:39-48 invokes panel initialization.
findings.sink: ApoRelaxLevelChooser.setMaxLevel(int) at ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:119-124 accepts the returned integer as the unlocked-level boundary.
findings.data_path: ApoRelaxApplet.init at ApoRelaxApplet.java:39-48 calls ApoRelaxPanel.init; ApoRelaxPanel.java:90-95 calls ApoHelp.loadData; ApoHelp.java:446-465 opens the HTTP connection and returns its first line; ApoRelaxPanel.java:94-95 parses it and passes it to setMaxLevel. ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:203-205 then renders levels through that boundary.
findings.attack_scenario: An on-path attacker intercepts the cleartext cookies.php request and returns the single line "11". The client parses it and displays all twelve built-in levels as unlocked, modifying the victim's progression without solving them. The same cleartext channel is used to save progress at ApoRelaxPanel.java:208-218.
findings.preconditions: The bundled JApplet entry point must be used so ApoConstants.B_APPLET is true, and the attacker must control apo-games.de or the victim's HTTP path. The normal desktop entry point leaves this branch disabled.
findings.validation_plan: Run the applet through a legacy JRE with an intercepting proxy. Return HTTP 200 and body "11\n" for /apoRelax/cookies.php. Open the level chooser and confirm that levels 1-12 are drawn as unlocked. Capturing the request also confirms that no TLS protects the response.

findings.title: Unbounded HTTP line read can exhaust or hang the applet
findings.code_excerpt:
BufferedReader iStream = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(con.getInputStream()));
retVal = iStream.readLine();
findings.entry_point: The response stream from the applet's progress endpoint, controlled by a malicious apo-games.de server or an HTTP on-path attacker.
findings.sink: BufferedReader.readLine() at ApoHelp.java:465 reads without a length bound, connect timeout, or read timeout.
findings.data_path: ApoRelaxApplet.java:48 calls ApoRelaxPanel.init; ApoRelaxPanel.java:93 invokes ApoHelp.loadData; ApoHelp.java:452-465 opens the connection and synchronously reads one unrestricted line before game startup continues. The same root cause appears in saveData at ApoHelp.java:424-436.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker returns an endless response body without a newline, or opens the response and stops sending data. Applet initialization remains blocked; if bytes continue arriving, readLine grows its buffer until the game process exhausts heap memory.
findings.preconditions: Applet mode must be used and the progress request must reach a malicious server or traverse an attacker-controlled plain-HTTP connection.
findings.validation_plan: Route www.apo-games.de through a test proxy/server that responds to /apoRelax/cookies.php with an endless chunked stream of 'A' bytes and no newline. Start the applet with a small heap such as -Xmx64m. A startup hang followed by increasing heap use or OutOfMemoryError confirms the issue.

findings.title: Editor decodes full-size images before enforcing its size cap
findings.entry_point: A local image selected through the desktop editor's file chooser at ApoRelaxEditor.java:221-226, including an image downloaded from an untrusted source.
findings.sink: ImageIO.read(File) decodes and allocates the complete attacker-specified raster before any dimension limit is applied.
findings.data_path: ApoRelaxEditor.loadImage at ApoRelaxEditor.java:221-226 gets the chosen path and calls ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.getImage; ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.java:513-515 delegates through ApoRelaxImages.getImage and ApoImageFromValue.getImageFromPath to ApoImage.getPic; ApoImage.java:88-94 performs ImageIO.read. Only after decoding returns does ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.java:491-507 scale dimensions above 400 pixels. The editor catches Exception at ApoRelaxEditor.java:227-229, not OutOfMemoryError.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker supplies a highly compressed PNG or similar accepted image whose header declares a very large raster and convinces the user to import it. ImageIO attempts to materialize the full raster, exhausting the game's heap or making it unresponsive before the 400-pixel scaling code runs.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode is required for the file chooser, the user must select the malicious image, and the configured heap must be smaller than the decoded raster.
findings.validation_plan: Create a valid, highly compressible 10000x10000 solid-color PNG, start the desktop game with -Xmx128m, enter Editor, and choose Load. An uncaught OutOfMemoryError or process hang occurring before a 400-pixel image is displayed proves the pre-scaling decode is exploitable.

findings.title: Locked levels remain clickable while hidden
findings.entry_point: Mouse press/release coordinates supplied by the local player while the level chooser is open.
findings.sink: ApoRelaxPanel.setGame(i) is invoked at ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:147 without checking i against maxLevel.
findings.data_path: ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:50-60 creates all twelve internal buttons and marks every one BVisible. ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:203-205 renders only indices through maxLevel, but mouseButtonReleased at lines 142-151 iterates the entire button list and starts any logically visible button. ApoRelaxPanel.java:144-151 then initializes the selected built-in level.
findings.attack_scenario: On a fresh game where only level 1 is drawn, a local user clicks the blank coordinate occupied by a hidden later-level button. The unchecked handler starts that locked level, bypassing progression without editing memory, files, or network traffic.
findings.preconditions: The level chooser must be open and the user must know or probe a hidden button's fixed coordinates.
findings.validation_plan: Start with maxLevel 0 and open the chooser. Click approximately (537,362), the center of button index 11 derived from ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:48-59. Confirm that setGame(11) starts level 12 even though only level 1 was rendered.

findings.title: Dormant URLClassLoader executes unauthenticated classes
findings.entry_point: There is no production entry point in ApoRelax. The public constructor parameters path and classname at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21 would be the input source, but a whole-tree reference search found no instantiation of ApoClassLoader.
findings.sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass followed by Class.newInstance at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75 loads and executes the selected class without signature or hash verification.
findings.data_path: A hypothetical caller supplies path and classname to ApoClassLoader.java:19-21 and invokes getMyClass. In applet mode, ApoClassLoader.java:65-69 treats path as a URL; lines 73-75 load and instantiate the class. No current menu, network response, command-line argument, or file parser calls this API.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical only: if this cloned helper is later wired to downloaded level or plugin metadata, an attacker hosts a class directory or JAR, supplies its URL and class name, and gains code execution through the class initializer or constructor. The present ApoRelax game offers no way to supply those values or invoke getMyClass.
findings.preconditions: A new or external caller must invoke the helper with attacker-controlled values; ApoConstants.B_APPLET must be true for an HTTP URL; and the runtime must permit URLClassLoader access. These conditions are not met by this variant.
findings.validation_plan: To prove the dormant primitive, build a test class whose static initializer writes a marker file, serve its package directory from a local HTTP server, set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true in a harness, and call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/", "test.Payload").getMyClass(). The marker proves execution; separately confirm that no ApoRelax source instantiates ApoClassLoader.

notes: All 56 Java files under the supplied root were reviewed; the corpus preserves the original prefix Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoRelax/. Findings 01 and 02 are applet-only: ApoRelaxApplet.java:27-29 sets B_APPLET, whereas ApoConstants.java:12 defaults it to false for ApoRelaxMain.java:17-32. ApoRelaxRandomLevels.java:25-26 has a tautologically true condition that returns a bundled image, making its plain-HTTP zufallsbild.com parser at lines 29-54 unreachable. ApoHighscore.java:69-194 and the HTTP constants at ApoConstants.java:21-22 are dormant because no game code calls ApoHighscore. ApoIO.java:18-105 has no subclass or call site in this variant. ApoHelp.getMd5Digest at ApoHelp.java:301-306 is unused, so MD5 does not protect any score, save, or level path. No ObjectInputStream/ObjectOutputStream, System.load/loadLibrary, native declaration, or .cheat/.mar/.skunk/.defence/.rep parser appears in this source tree.
